classes.label: SI units
classes.qa: Which of the following is the SI unit of {k}?
classes.qb: {v} is the SI unit of which physical quantity?
classes.qo: State the SI unit of {k}.
classes.src: NEB/CEE/IOE physics: SI base and derived units (BIPM SI brochure)
pairs: The SI unit of force is the newton, the force that gives a 1 kg mass an acceleration of $1\ \text{m s}^{-2}$.
The SI unit of work and energy is the joule; one joule is one newton-metre.
The SI unit of power is the watt; one watt is one joule per second.
The SI unit of electric charge is the coulomb; one coulomb is one ampere-second.
The SI unit of electric current is the ampere, a base SI unit.
The SI unit of potential difference is the volt; one volt is one joule per coulomb.
The SI unit of electrical resistance is the ohm; one ohm is one volt per ampere.
The SI unit of capacitance is the farad; one farad is one coulomb per volt.
The SI unit of magnetic flux is the weber; one weber is one volt-second.
The SI unit of magnetic flux density is the tesla; one tesla is one weber per square metre.
The SI unit of inductance is the henry; one henry is one weber per ampere.
The SI unit of frequency is the hertz; one hertz is one cycle per second.
The SI unit of pressure is the pascal; one pascal is one newton per square metre.
The SI unit of thermodynamic temperature is the kelvin, a base SI unit.
The SI unit of amount of substance is the mole, a base SI unit.
The SI unit of luminous intensity is the candela, a base SI unit.
The SI unit of radioactivity is the becquerel; one becquerel is one disintegration per second.
The SI unit of absorbed radiation dose is the gray; one gray is one joule per kilogram.
The SI unit of solid angle is the steradian, a dimensionless derived unit.
The SI unit of electrical conductance is the siemens; one siemens is one ampere per volt.

classes.label: Dimensions
classes.qa: Which of the following is the dimensional formula of {k}?
classes.qb: {v} is the dimensional formula of which physical quantity?
classes.qo: Write the dimensional formula of {k}.
pairs: Force is mass times acceleration, so its dimensional formula is $[MLT^{-2}]$.
Work is force times displacement, so its dimensional formula is $[ML^{2}T^{-2}]$.
Power is work per unit time, so its dimensional formula is $[ML^{2}T^{-3}]$.
Pressure is force per unit area, so its dimensional formula is $[ML^{-1}T^{-2}]$.
Momentum is mass times velocity, so its dimensional formula is $[MLT^{-1}]$.
Acceleration is velocity per unit time, so its dimensional formula is $[LT^{-2}]$.
Velocity is displacement per unit time, so its dimensional formula is $[LT^{-1}]$.
Density is mass per unit volume, so its dimensional formula is $[ML^{-3}]$.
Surface tension is force per unit length, so its dimensional formula is $[MT^{-2}]$.
Viscosity is tangential force per unit area per unit velocity gradient, so its dimensional formula is $[ML^{-1}T^{-1}]$.
Planck's constant is energy divided by frequency, so its dimensional formula is $[ML^{2}T^{-1}]$.
From $F=Gm_{1}m_{2}/r^{2}$ the gravitational constant has dimensions $[M^{-1}L^{3}T^{-2}]$.
Specific heat capacity is heat per unit mass per kelvin, so its dimensional formula is $[L^{2}T^{-2}K^{-1}]$.
Electric field is force per unit charge, so its dimensional formula is $[MLT^{-3}A^{-1}]$.
Potential is work per unit charge, so its dimensional formula is $[ML^{2}T^{-3}A^{-1}]$.
Resistance is potential difference per unit current, so its dimensional formula is $[ML^{2}T^{-3}A^{-2}]$.
Capacitance is charge per unit potential, so its dimensional formula is $[M^{-1}L^{-2}T^{4}A^{2}]$.
Magnetic flux is field times area, so its dimensional formula is $[ML^{2}T^{-2}A^{-1}]$.

the law of electrostatic force between point charges

Ohm's law, $V=IR$, is named after Georg Simon Ohm.
Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction is named after Michael Faraday.
the circuital law relating current and magnetic field

the law giving the magnetic field of a current element

the two circuit laws for current and voltage

the law fixing the direction of an induced current
Lenz's law is named after Heinrich Lenz.
the law of heating by an electric current
Joule's law of heating is named after James Prescott Joule.
the law relating recession speed and distance of galaxies
Hubble's law is named after Edwin Hubble.
the change of observed frequency due to relative motion
The Doppler effect is named after Christian Doppler.
the explanation of the photoelectric effect

the exclusion principle for electrons in an atom
The Pauli exclusion principle was proposed by Wolfgang Pauli.

classes.qo: Classify {k} as a scalar or a vector quantity.
pairs: Force has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector quantity.
Displacement has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector quantity.
Velocity has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector quantity.
Acceleration has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector quantity.
Momentum has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector quantity.
Torque has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector quantity.
Electric field intensity has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector quantity.
Impulse has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector quantity.
Mass has magnitude only, so it is a scalar quantity.
Distance has magnitude only, so it is a scalar quantity.
Speed has magnitude only, so it is a scalar quantity.
Work is the scalar product of force and displacement, so it is a scalar quantity.
Energy has magnitude only, so it is a scalar quantity.
Power has magnitude only, so it is a scalar quantity.
Pressure has magnitude only, so it is a scalar quantity.
Temperature has magnitude only, so it is a scalar quantity.
Electric current has magnitude and a sense of flow but does not obey vector addition, so it is treated as a scalar quantity.
Magnetic flux is a scalar product of two vectors, so it is a scalar quantity.

classes.qo: Write the main function of {v}.

intracellular digestion and hydrolysis of worn-out organelles
Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes and digest worn-out organelles, so they are called suicidal bags.
modification, sorting and packaging of proteins
The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts and packages proteins for secretion.
synthesis of lipids and detoxification in liver cells
The smooth endoplasmic reticulum synthesises lipids and detoxifies drugs in liver cells.
The chloroplast contains chlorophyll and is the site of photosynthesis.
maintenance of turgor pressure and storage of cell sap
The central vacuole stores cell sap and maintains turgor pressure in plant cells.
organisation of the spindle during animal cell division
The centriole organises spindle fibres during animal cell division.
oxidation of fatty acids and breakdown of hydrogen peroxide
Peroxisomes oxidise fatty acids and break down hydrogen peroxide using catalase.

the alpha cells of the islets of Langerhans of the pancreas

Thyroxine is secreted by the thyroid gland and controls the basal metabolic rate.

Lack of vitamin D causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.
Lack of vitamin E causes haemolysis of red blood cells.

Ascariasis is caused by the roundworm Ascaris lumbricoides.

classes.label: Genetics terminology

pairs: the set of genes present in an organism
The genotype is the genetic constitution of an organism.
the observable characteristics of an organism
The phenotype is the observable expression of the genotype.
the alternative forms of a gene at one locus
Alleles are alternative forms of the same gene at a locus.
an organism with two identical alleles for a trait
A homozygous organism carries two identical alleles for a trait.
an organism with two different alleles for a trait
A heterozygous organism carries two different alleles for a trait.
a cross with a homozygous recessive parent to reveal a genotype
A test cross is made with a homozygous recessive parent to reveal the genotype.
the allele that expresses itself in the heterozygous state
A dominant allele expresses its phenotype in the heterozygous state.
the allele masked in the heterozygous state
A recessive allele is masked in the heterozygous state and expresses only when homozygous.
the transmission of traits from parents to offspring
Heredity is the transmission of traits from parents to offspring.
a change in the nucleotide sequence of DNA
A mutation is a change in the nucleotide sequence of DNA.
the exchange of segments between homologous chromosomes
Crossing over exchanges segments between homologous chromosomes during meiosis.
a three-base code in mRNA that specifies an amino acid
A codon is a three-base sequence of mRNA that specifies an amino acid.

all the populations living together in an area
A community is all the populations that live together in an area.
the community together with its physical environment
An ecosystem is a community together with its non-living environment.
the place where an organism lives
A habitat is the place where an organism lives.
the role an organism plays in its ecosystem
The ecological niche is the functional role of an organism in its ecosystem.
organisms that make their own food by photosynthesis

organisms that feed on other organisms

organisms that break down dead organic matter
Decomposers break down dead organic matter and release nutrients.
the transition zone between two ecosystems

the variety of life in an ecosystem
Biodiversity is the variety of species, genes and ecosystems in an area.

classes.src: NEB/SEE/CEE mathematics: standard results and mensuration
pairs: the area of a circle of radius $r$
The area of a circle is $\pi r^{2}$.
the circumference of a circle of radius $r$
The circumference of a circle is $2\pi r$.
the volume of a sphere of radius $r$
The volume of a sphere is $\frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}$.
the surface area of a sphere of radius $r$
The surface area of a sphere is $4\pi r^{2}$.
the area of a triangle with base $b$ and height $h$
The area of a triangle is $\frac{1}{2}bh$.
the volume of a cylinder of radius $r$ and height $h$
The volume of a cylinder is $\pi r^{2}h$.
the curved surface area of a cylinder of radius $r$ and height $h$
The curved surface area of a cylinder is $2\pi rh$.
the volume of a cone of radius $r$ and height $h$
The volume of a cone is $\frac{1}{3}\pi r^{2}h$.
the distance between two points $(x_{1},y_{1})$ and $(x_{2},y_{2})$
The distance between two points is $\sqrt{(x_{2}-x_{1})^{2}+(y_{2}-y_{1})^{2}}$.
the slope of the line through $(x_{1},y_{1})$ and $(x_{2},y_{2})$
The slope of a line through two points is $(y_{2}-y_{1})/(x_{2}-x_{1})$.
the sum of the roots of $ax^{2}+bx+c=0$
The sum of the roots of $ax^{2}+bx+c=0$ is $-b/a$.
the product of the roots of $ax^{2}+bx+c=0$
The product of the roots of $ax^{2}+bx+c=0$ is $c/a$.
the sum of the first $n$ natural numbers
The sum of the first $n$ natural numbers is $\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$.
the sum of the first $n$ terms of an arithmetic progression
The sum of $n$ terms of an AP is $\frac{n}{2}[2a+(n-1)d]$.
the sum of the first $n$ terms of a geometric progression
The sum of $n$ terms of a GP is $\frac{a(r^{n}-1)}{r-1}$ for $r\neq 1$.
The arithmetic mean of $a$ and $b$ is $\frac{a+b}{2}$.
The geometric mean of $a$ and $b$ is $\sqrt{ab}$.
the sine rule in a triangle
The sine rule is $\frac{a}{\sin A}=\frac{b}{\sin B}=\frac{c}{\sin C}$.
the cosine rule in a triangle
